headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing context if paired with a local course repo that users may feed into it; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are otherwise limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a static open-source course repo with no runtime channel; Profile B is a vendor-hosted search agent that can browse and ingest uploaded documents. A direct injection path is not documented, but if users copy A’s content into B or upload course materials, malicious text could influence B’s browsing/output. The bridge is user-mediated, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is manually pasted or uploaded into agent_b
IF agent_b treats uploaded document text as instructions during browsing or answer synthesis
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted course text into agent_b
Use a prompt wrapper that labels uploaded content as data only
Review agent_b outputs before reuse in downstream tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for uploaded content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no network egress, but agent B is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded PDFs/images plus browsing context. If users place sensitive material from A’s workspace into B, that data can flow to a third-party backend. The pair does not show a shared filesystem, so leakage is indirect, but the default vendor-hosted processing makes the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive files from agent_a are uploaded into agent_b
IF agent_b retains browsing context or uploaded-document content in vendor systems
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or regulated data to agent_b
Strip identifiers before upload
Use a local-only alternative for sensitive documents
Review vendor retention settings in agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or execution surfaces, while agent B cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell commands. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is conceptual work on data-engineering content and browser-based analysis, so the pair’s mutable-resource contention is minimal.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access not shown in the profiles
IF a shared mutable workspace is introduced outside the documented surfaces
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for shared artifacts
Avoid giving agent_b filesystem write access
Separate git and workspace ownership
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable store is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s answer-engine workflow can treat retrieved or uploaded content as authoritative, and agent A is a course repo whose material may be reused as source text. If A-derived content is fed into B without verification, B can propagate errors or stale facts into downstream answers. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF agent_a content is used as source material for agent_b answers
IF agent_b outputs are reused without human verification
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse
Compare B outputs against primary sources
Mark A content as educational, not authoritative
Review high-impact answers manually
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for agent A, and agent B’s privacy policy/docs are cited but not specific to a regulated data class here. Because the pair lacks evidence of sensitive-data handling, compliance risk is limited to general policy mismatch if users upload regulated content into B. The other agent is not cited beyond its open-source status because no residency claim is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into agent_b
IF agent_b retention or residency terms conflict with the data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in agent_b
Check vendor privacy terms before upload
Use anonymized excerpts only
Document allowed data classes for the pair
requires-engineering: route regulated data to a compliant local workflow
